title: Clinical Review Desk Note on Expedited Appeals and Grievances Cases
content:
**Appeals and Grievances**: when a case runs on the expedited timeframe, and what happens to a case whose expedite request is refused.

## Rule

A case is expedited where the case type offers an expedited timeframe and the treating provider indicates, or the plan finds, that the standard timeframe could seriously jeopardize the member's life, health or ability to regain maximum function. A refused expedite request moves the case to Standard Appeal with the standard due date counted from the original filed date, with prompt oral notice and written notice within the case type's refusal-notice period.

## Condition, judgement, result

| Input | Judgement | Result |
|---|---|---|
| The case type offers an expedited timeframe, and the treating provider indicates that the standard timeframe could seriously jeopardize the member's life, health or ability to regain maximum function | Both parts are met | The case is expedited |
| The case type offers an expedited timeframe, and the plan finds the same jeopardy | Both parts are met | The case is expedited |
| The expedite request is refused | Refusal | The case moves to Standard Appeal; its due date becomes the standard due date counted from the original filed date; prompt oral notice is given, and written notice follows within the refusal-notice period |

## Points of judgement

- **Who may supply the jeopardy finding.** Either the treating provider's indication or the plan's own finding is enough; both are not needed.
- **The three interests protected.** The jeopardy concerns the member's life, the member's health, or the member's ability to regain maximum function; any one of them suffices.
- **Due date after a refusal.** The standard period runs from the original filed date of the case, not from the day the expedite request was refused.
- **Records of a refusal.** The case type on record changes to Standard Appeal, the due date changes to the standard due date, and an expedite denial notice letter is logged.

## Hypothetical illustration

A case filed on a given day D carries an expedite request, and the plan refuses that request. The case becomes a Standard Appeal whose standard due date is counted from D; oral notice of the refusal is given promptly and written notice follows within the refusal-notice period counted from the day of the refusal.
